function.name: Movies_3_FindMovies
function.description: Retrieves a list of movies based on the director, genre, and cast specified by the user. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directed_by.description: Director of the movie. Use 'dontcare' if the director is not a specific search criterion.

genre.description: Genre of the movie. Use 'dontcare' to include all genres or genre is not specified by user

cast.description: Names of leading actors or actresses in the movie. Use 'dontcare' if the cast is not a specific search criterion.

message.reasoning:
User wants a movie in "Imaginative fiction" genre. The function only supports certain genres: Offbeat, Fantasy, World, Mystery, Thriller, Comedy, Comedy-drama, Horror, Animation, Sci-fi, Cult, Drama, Anime, Family, Action, dontcare. There's no "Imaginative fiction". We can interpret "Imaginative fiction" as maybe "Fantasy" or "Sci-fi" or "Fantasy-type". The user says they have started to watch a lot of fantasy-type movies lately. So we can recommend a fantasy movie. We can ask clarifying question: "Do you want a fantasy movie?" But we can also guess. The user says "I would like to find a movie to watch in the Imaginative fiction genre, as I have started to watch a lot of fantasy-type movies lately, you know!!!!!!"

We can respond: "Sure! Since you enjoy fantasy-type movies, here are some recommendations." Then we can call the function with genre "Fantasy". We don't need director or cast. So we call function with directed_by: "dontcare", genre: "Fantasy", cast: "dontcare". That will return a list of movies. Then we can present them. Let's do that.
